steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported and available for use.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building React components with state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported React, but don't forget to also import the useState hook.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main Authentication component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Authentication that returns an empty fragment (<> </>) initially.
steps.hint: Define the component using either function Authentication() {} or const Authentication = () => {}. Return an empty fragment with <> </>.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and useState here

// Create the Authentication component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The Authentication component is defined and returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: A functional component named Authentication is defined and returns an empty fragment (<> </>).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main Authentication component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a component, but make sure it's named exactly 'Authentication' and returns an empty fragment (<> </>).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a functional component named Authentication that returns an empty fragment.

steps.title: Initialize authentication state
steps.instruction: Inside your Authentication component, use useState to declare an isAuthenticated state variable initialized to false.
steps.hint: Call useState with false as the initial value and destructure the returned array into isAuthenticated and setIsAuthenticated.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has an isAuthenticated state variable that tracks whether the user is logged in.
successCriteria: isAuthenticated state is declared using useState with false as the initial value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully set up the authentication state. The isAuthenticated variable will help track the user's login status throughout the component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've correctly initialized isAuthenticated to false using useState.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on this step: use useState to create an isAuthenticated state variable initialized to false inside the Authentication component.

steps.title: Initialize user role state
steps.instruction: Inside your Authentication component, use useState to create a state variable named userRole and initialize it to the string 'guest'.
steps.hint: Add a second useState call after your existing isAuthenticated state. Remember to destructure the array: const [userRole, setUserRole] = useState('guest');
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing a role state
const [userRole, setUserRole] = useState('guest');
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have two state variables: isAuthenticated and userRole, with userRole initialized to 'guest'.
successCriteria: The userRole state variable is declared with useState and initialized to 'guest'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added userRole state to track authorization levels. This will allow us to implement role-based access control.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've properly declared the userRole state variable with useState and initialized it to 'guest'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Please add a userRole state variable using useState and initialize it to 'guest' inside your Authentication component.

steps.title: Define login handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the Authentication component, define a function named handleLogin that sets isAuthenticated to true and userRole to 'user'.
steps.hint: Write a function that updates both state variables when called.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleLogin function is defined that will authenticate the user and assign a default role.
successCriteria: The handleLogin function is defined and sets isAuthenticated to true and userRole to 'user'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the login handler that will manage authentication state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it sets both isAuthenticated to true and userRole to 'user'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleLogin function is missing or doesn't set the required state values.

steps.title: Define logout handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the Authentication component, define a function named handleLogout that sets isAuthenticated to false and userRole to 'guest'.
steps.hint: Create a function that updates both state variables to represent a logged-out user.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleLogout function is defined that updates authentication and role state.
successCriteria: The handleLogout function sets isAuthenticated to false and userRole to 'guest'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a logout handler that properly resets the authentication state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it sets both isAuthenticated to false and userRole to 'guest'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The logout handler isn't defined correctly. Create a function named handleLogout that updates both state variables.

steps.title: Define admin upgrade handler
steps.instruction: Inside your Authentication component, define a function named handleUpgradeToAdmin that sets the userRole state to 'admin' when the user is authenticated.
steps.hint: Create a function that checks if the user is authenticated, then updates the userRole state to 'admin'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleUpgradeToAdmin function is defined and ready to be used for authorization changes.
successCriteria: The handleUpgradeToAdmin function is defined, checks isAuthenticated, and sets userRole to 'admin'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the authorization upgrade handler. This function demonstrates how authenticated users can have their roles elevated.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it checks isAuthenticated and sets userRole to 'admin' when authenticated.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Create a function named handleUpgradeToAdmin that updates userRole to 'admin' when isAuthenticated is true.

steps.title: Add authentication status display
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a paragraph element that displays the current authentication status using the isAuthenticated state.
steps.hint:
Use JSX to create a

tag and embed the isAuthenticated state value inside curly braces to show it as text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now display a paragraph showing whether the user is authenticated (true/false) based on the current state.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added to the return statement that displays the value of isAuthenticated.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a paragraph that shows the current authentication status.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but make sure it displays the isAuthenticated state value using curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element is missing or doesn't display the isAuthenticated state correctly.

steps.title: Add user role display
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your Authentication component, add a paragraph element that displays the current userRole value.
steps.hint: Use JSX to create a paragraph element and embed the userRole state variable inside curly braces.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a state variable in JSX

Current role: {userRole}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a paragraph displaying the current user role, which defaults to 'user'.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added inside the return statement that displays the userRole state value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a paragraph that displays the current user role, making the authorization level visible to users.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but make sure it displays the userRole state variable using curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element displaying the userRole value is missing or incorrect. Check that you're using the correct state variable name and JSX syntax.

steps.title: Add authentication controls and wire event handlers
steps.instruction: Add a login button wired to handleLogin, a logout button wired to handleLogout, and an upgrade button wired to handleUpgradeToAdmin (with conditional rendering based on authentication status) inside your component's return statement.
steps.hint: Use JSX button elements with onClick handlers. For conditional rendering, you can use logical && operator or ternary expressions.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component should render three interactive buttons for authentication and authorization actions, with conditional rendering based on the isAuthenticated state.
successCriteria: Login button calls handleLogin when clicked
Logout button calls handleLogout when clicked
Upgrade button calls handleUpgradeToAdmin when clicked
Buttons are conditionally rendered based on isAuthenticated
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added authentication controls with proper event handling and conditional rendering.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some buttons, but check if all three are present with correct onClick handlers and conditional rendering.
steps.feedbackWrong: The authentication controls are missing or incorrectly implemented. Review the requirements for all three buttons with proper event handlers.
